title: An Improved Fit for Linear Halo Bias at High Redshift
comment: 6 pages + references, 3 figures, Fig. 3 and Eq. 8 are the main results. To be submitted to PRL, comments are welcome
summary: High- to ultrahigh-redshift clustering of halos provides a powerful tool to understand cosmology and galaxy formation. However, theoretical predictions are not firmly established in the first billion years, where current and upcoming surveys are beginning to reach percent-level precision. Here we measure dark matter halo biases at $z=6$ - 19 from simulation data, and find they are $\sim$ 3 - 4$\%$ higher than canonical results calibrated at low $z$. We provide an updated linear-bias fit at these early times, reducing the mean systematic offset to $< 1\%$. These results will enable robust interpretation of early-Universe galaxy clustering from JWST, Roman, and intensity-mapping surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper recalibrates dark matter halo biases at redshifts 6 to 19 using simulations, improving upon low-redshift models to achieve under 1% systematic error, thereby aiding next-generation early-Universe galaxy clustering analyses.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to improve theoretical predictions of dark matter halo clustering bias in the first billion years (high to ultrahigh redshift) due to upcoming surveys reaching percent-level precision.
AI.method: The authors measure dark matter halo biases at redshifts 6 to 19 using simulation data, comparing results to canonical low-redshift calibrations.
AI.result: They find halo biases at these early epochs are approximately 3-4% higher than previous calibrations, and provide an updated linear-bias fit that reduces systematic offset to less than 1%.
AI.conclusion: The updated bias measurements enable more accurate interpretation of galaxy clustering in the early Universe from forthcoming JWST, Roman, and intensity-mapping surveys.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: A Test of the Gravitational Force Law on Cosmological Scales Using the Kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich Effect
comment: Published in Physical Review Letters
summary: The mean pairwise velocity of massive halos reflects the gravitational force law on cosmic scales. We combine cosmic microwave background intensity maps from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope and a galaxy catalog from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey to estimate the mean pairwise velocity using the kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect. On scales from 30 -- 230 megaparsecs, we constrain the gravitational acceleration between pairs of halos at separation $r$ to be $g\propto 1/r^n$ with $n=2.1\pm 0.3$, which is consistent with Newtonian gravity in an expanding spacetime (\textit{i.e.}, the standard $Λ$CDM model). This constraint shows agreement with an inverse quadratic radial dependence over the large distances separating galaxy halos, as expected in standard cosmology. Upcoming surveys have the potential to rule out $n = 1$ at $10σ$ significance. Our results establish the kSZ effect as a powerful tool for testing gravity on cosmological scales.

AI.tldr: By measuring halo pairwise velocities via the kSZ effect, the study confirms that gravity follows an inverse-square law on scales of 30–230 Mpc, validating standard cosmology and demonstrating the kSZ effect as a valuable tool for testing gravity on cosmic scales.
AI.motivation: To test the gravitational force law on cosmological scales by measuring the mean pairwise velocity of massive halos using the kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect.
AI.method: Combining cosmic microwave background intensity maps from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope with a galaxy catalog from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey to estimate the mean pairwise velocity of halos and constrain the gravitational acceleration as a function of separation distance.
AI.result: The gravitational acceleration between halo pairs follows a power law $g \propto 1/r^n$ with $n=2.1 \pm 0.3$, consistent with Newtonian gravity under the standard $\Lambda$CDM model; future surveys may rule out alternative power laws with high significance.
AI.conclusion: The kSZ effect provides a powerful observational probe to confirm the inverse-square law of gravity on large cosmological scales, supporting the standard cosmological model and enabling precise tests of gravitational physics.

title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Handling Uncertainties and Distribution Shifts for Precision Cosmology
comment: Whitepaper for the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge Competition. More info is available at our GitHub repository https://github.com/FAIR-Universe/Cosmology_Challenge. 13 pages, 5 figures, 1 table
summary: Weak gravitational lensing, the correlated distortion of background galaxy shapes by foreground structures, is a powerful probe of the matter distribution in our universe and allows accurate constraints on the cosmological model. In recent years, high-order statistics and machine learning (ML) techniques have been applied to weak lensing data to extract the nonlinear information beyond traditional two-point analysis. However, these methods typically rely on cosmological simulations, which poses several challenges: simulations are computationally expensive, limiting most realistic setups to a low training data regime; inaccurate modeling of systematics in the simulations create distribution shifts that can bias cosmological parameter constraints; and varying simulation setups across studies make method comparison difficult. To address these difficulties, we present the first weak lensing benchmark dataset with several realistic systematics and launch the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge. The challenge focuses on measuring the fundamental properties of the universe from weak lensing data with limited training set and potential distribution shifts, while providing a standardized benchmark for rigorous comparison across methods. Organized in two phases, the challenge will bring together the physics and ML communities to advance the methodologies for handling systematic uncertainties, data efficiency, and distribution shifts in weak lensing analysis with ML, ultimately facilitating the deployment of ML approaches into upcoming weak lensing survey analysis.

AI.tldr: Introduces a benchmark dataset and community ML challenge to improve weak lensing analysis by addressing simulation limitations, systematics, and data efficiency, promoting collaboration between physics and ML experts.
AI.motivation: Current weak gravitational lensing analyses using high-order statistics and ML techniques face challenges due to computational expense of simulations, systematics-induced distribution shifts, and inconsistent simulation setups hindering method comparison.
AI.method: Develop a benchmark dataset incorporating realistic systematics for weak lensing and launch the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge, organized in two phases to encourage community engagement in addressing systematic uncertainties, data limitations, and distribution shifts.
AI.result: The challenge provides a standardized platform for rigorous comparison across methods, fostering collaborations between physics and ML communities to improve methodology for systematic uncertainties and data efficiency in weak lensing analysis.
AI.conclusion: The establishment of a realistic benchmark dataset and community challenge advances ML methodologies in weak lensing, enabling more reliable cosmological parameter constraints and facilitating ML deployment in upcoming surveys.

title: Forecasting neutrino mass constraints from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
comment: 12 pages,5 figures
summary: We present realistic forecasts for the constraining power of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on fundamental cosmological parameters, with particular emphasis on the absolute neutrino mass scale, using full-shape analyzes of the galaxy power spectrum. We analyze simulated lightcone mock catalogs of H$α$ emission-line galaxies spanning the redshift range $0.5 < z < 2$ over $2400\ \mathrm{deg}^2$, designed to reproduce the expected properties of the Roman High Latitude Wide Area Spectroscopic Survey. We perform parameter inference on the galaxy power spectrum multipoles using two complementary theoretical frameworks: a model-dependent approach based on the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFT of LSS) within $Λ$CDM, and a model-independent phenomenological approach that makes no assumptions about the background cosmological model. In the $Λ$CDM analysis, we find $m_ν< 0.380(0.162)\ \mathrm{eV}$ at $95(68)\%$ C.L. using Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) prior and a broad prior on $n_s$, which tightens to $m_ν< 0.276(0.121)\ \mathrm{eV}$ when Planck priors on $ω_b$, $ω_\mathrm{cdm}$, and $n_s$ are added. Our forecasts show that Roman can additionally constrain $H_0$, $Ω_m$, and $σ_8$ with precisions of $1.3\%$, $4.3\%$, and $2.9\%$ in line with Stage IV galaxy survey measurements and forecasts. In the model-independent analysis, we demonstrate that the phenomenological model can robustly recover unbiased measurements of the angular diameter distance, the Hubble parameter, and the growth of structure across all redshift bins, in the same range of scales as the EFT model, and obtain $m_ν< 0.63(0.36)\ \mathrm{eV}$ at $95(68)\%$ C.L. when Planck priors are included.

AI.tldr: This paper forecasts the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's capability to constrain neutrino masses and cosmological parameters using galaxy power spectrum analyses with both model-dependent EFT and model-independent approaches, showing competitive and robust constraints.
AI.motivation: To forecast how effectively the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope can constrain fundamental cosmological parameters, particularly the absolute neutrino mass scale, using realistic galaxy survey data and complementary theoretical models.
AI.method: The study uses simulated lightcone mock catalogs of Hα emission-line galaxies from 0.5<z<2 over 2400 deg², analyzing the full-shape galaxy power spectrum multipoles. Two theoretical frameworks are employed: (1) a model-dependent Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure within ΛCDM, and (2) a model-independent phenomenological approach without background cosmology assumptions. Parameter inference incorporates priors from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis and Planck measurements.
AI.result: In the ΛCDM model-dependent analysis, neutrino mass constraints improve to mν < 0.276(0.121) eV at 95(68)% C.L. with Planck priors, along with percent-level precision measurements of H₀ (1.3%), Ω_m (4.3%), and σ_8 (2.9%). The phenomenological model independently obtains mν < 0.63(0.36) eV at 95(68)% C.L. with Planck priors while reliably recovering angular diameter distance, Hubble parameter, and growth of structure across redshifts.
AI.conclusion: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will significantly constrain cosmological parameters, notably providing upper limits on the absolute neutrino mass scale and measuring the Hubble constant, matter density, and structure growth with high precision. Both model-dependent and model-independent methods yield robust and complementary cosmological constraints.

title: Consistent Treatment of Muons in Binary Neutron Star Mergers
comment: 12+7 pages, 5 figures. Intended for APJL Comments are most welcome
summary: We present a set of numerical-relativity binary neutron star merger simulations incorporating muons and muonic reactions for two baseline baryonic equations-of-state. In order to investigate the possible impact of muons and muonic weak reactions, we treat neutrinos with a gray (energy-independent) truncated moments scheme and an implicit-explicit time integrator. Newly computed neutrino rates are employed within the full kinematics approach for a set of relevant reactions, and pair-processes are modeled via opacities computed using reaction kernels, that allow a consistent treatment of neutrino interaction rates. We find that equilibration between matter and radiation is successfully captured by a novel two timescales approach. Of astrophysical interest is the general agreement between our muonic and non-muonic results regarding the remnant evolution, disk and outflow properties. Average electron fractions, asymptotic velocities and temperatures are different by less than $\sim 6\%$, while the main impact of muons is a reduction in ejecta masses by at most $\sim 17\%$. Therefore, based on our findings, accounting for the presence of muons and muonic reactions might result much less severe consequences regarding nucleosynthetic yields and electromagnetic counterparts than previously reported in the literature.

AI.tldr: Simulations including muons in neutron star mergers show minor changes in key astrophysical properties, indicating muons have a less severe effect on ejecta and emitted signals than earlier studies suggested.
AI.motivation: To investigate the impact of muons and muonic weak reactions on binary neutron star merger simulations, which were previously uncertain.
AI.method: Numerical-relativity simulations incorporating muons and muonic reactions using a gray neutrino transport scheme with implicit-explicit time integration, new neutrino rates with full kinematics, and pair-processes with reaction kernels for consistent neutrino interaction treatment.
AI.result: Muon effects cause less than ~6% differences in electron fractions, velocities, and temperatures, with up to ~17% reduction in ejecta masses; overall remnant evolution and outflow properties are similar with or without muons.
AI.conclusion: Inclusion of muons and muonic reactions has a milder impact on nucleosynthetic yields and electromagnetic counterparts of neutron star mergers than previously thought.

title: Closing the Observational Gap in Cosmic Dynamics: AI-Enabled Reconstruction of the Universe's Vorticity and Rotational Flow Morphology
comment: 18 pages, 9 figures
summary: The cosmic vorticity field, an essential tracer of nonlinear structure formation, has remained observationally inaccessible because transverse galaxy motions are difficult to measure and analytic models struggle to capture shell-crossing. Here we report an empirical reconstruction of this field by applying an artificial intelligence framework trained on simulations of the concordance LambdaCDM model to Sloan Digital Sky Survey galaxies. The recovered three-dimensional velocity and vorticity fields reveal coherent vortical structures, including spiral flows in clusters, filaments, and voids, and the cosmic web inferred from vorticity closely matches that derived from density segmentation. The power spectra of the reconstructed velocity and vorticity fields agree statistically with LambdaCDM predictions, and the inferred velocity field effectively removes redshift-space distortions, yielding an almost isotropic clustering signal. These converging lines of evidence, obtained from an independent perspective, reinforce the concordance cosmological model. By closing a long-standing observational gap, our results highlight the potential of AI-driven reconstruction to access otherwise unobservable quantities and to address fundamental questions in cosmology and galaxy formation.

AI.tldr: Using AI trained on simulations, the paper reconstructs the cosmic vorticity field from galaxy survey data, revealing structures consistent with LambdaCDM predictions and removing observational distortions, thereby supporting the standard cosmological model.
AI.motivation: The cosmic vorticity field is a crucial but observationally inaccessible tracer of nonlinear structure formation due to the difficulty of measuring transverse galaxy motions and limitations of analytic models in capturing shell-crossing.
AI.method: An artificial intelligence framework trained on simulations of the LambdaCDM model was applied to Sloan Digital Sky Survey galaxy data to empirically reconstruct the three-dimensional cosmic vorticity and velocity fields.
AI.result: The reconstructed fields reveal coherent vortical structures consistent with the cosmic web, with power spectra matching LambdaCDM predictions. The inferred velocity field removes redshift-space distortions, producing an almost isotropic clustering signal, thus providing observational evidence supporting the concordance cosmological model.
AI.conclusion: AI-driven reconstruction successfully recovers the cosmic vorticity field, bridging an observational gap and validating the LambdaCDM model from an independent perspective, highlighting the method's potential for probing unobservable cosmological quantities and advancing galaxy formation studies.

title: Constraining Quintessential Inflation with ACT: A Gauss-Bonnet Gateway
comment: 9 pages
summary:
Recent results from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), indicating a higher and more tightly constrained scalar spectral index, $n_s = 0.9743 \pm 0.0034$, place several inflationary models under tension, with quintessential inflation pushed close to or beyond the $2σ$ boundary in the $r$--$n_s$ plane. In this work, we revisit quintessential inflation within the framework of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet (EGB) gravity, where a scalar field non-minimally coupled to the Gauss--Bonnet invariant modifies the inflationary dynamics.
  We consider three representative coupling functions -- exponential, hyperbolic secant, and hyperbolic tangent -- and show that the exponential and sech-type couplings can shift the predicted values of $r$ and $n_s$ into the $1σ$ region allowed by ACT, thereby restoring consistency with observations. In contrast, the tanh-type coupling remains disfavored, underscoring the sensitivity of inflationary observables to the coupling structure.
  We further investigate the reheating phase using a model-independent parametrization and demonstrate that viable thermal histories can be realized even in the absence of a potential minimum, with reheating temperatures consistent with Big Bang nucleosynthesis bounds. Overall, our analysis shows that EGB corrections provide a viable and robust extension that reconciles quintessential inflation with current precision cosmological data, and we identify the corresponding allowed parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits quintessential inflation within Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, showing that certain scalar-Gauss--Bonnet couplings can align inflation predictions with ACT data, and that viable reheating scenarios are achievable, making the extended model consistent with current cosmological observations.
AI.motivation: Recent precise measurements from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope resulted in tighter constraints on the scalar spectral index, putting traditional quintessential inflation models under tension; the work aims to explore if EGB gravity corrections can reconcile these models with observations.
AI.method: The study analyzes quintessential inflation models incorporating scalar fields non-minimally coupled to the Gauss--Bonnet invariant with three types of coupling functions (exponential, hyperbolic secant, and hyperbolic tangent), examining their effects on inflationary observables (r and n_s) and reheating dynamics.
AI.result: Exponential and sech-type couplings shift the tensor-to-scalar ratio and spectral index predictions into observationally favored regions, whereas the tanh-type coupling does not; the model supports feasible reheating temperatures consistent with Big Bang nucleosynthesis even without a potential minimum, identifying an allowed parameter space within EGB framework.
AI.conclusion: Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity modifications allow quintessential inflation models to be consistent with recent precise cosmological data from ACT by adjusting inflationary observables within the 1σ allowed region and supporting viable reheating scenarios.

title: The azimuthal structure of magnetically arrested disks during flux eruption events
comment: 12 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: We analyze data from a standard 3D general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulation, focusing on equatorial slices in order to examine the details and the evolution of the azimuthal structure of the accreting matter. During flux eruption events, the non-axisymmetric features of the equatorial inner accretion disk are considerably enhanced, with this enhancement being more prominent close to the black hole. Our analysis of the azimuthal structure of the equatorial accretion disk finds that the matter distribution in the vicinity of the horizon is dominated by low azimuthal mode numbers, specifically by the $m = 2$, and $m = 1$ modes, indicating that the non-axisymmetry of the disk during flux eruption events is enhanced due to the emergence of features with a large angular size on the equatorial plane. Our results suggest that the morphology of the equatorial accretion flow close to the black hole is mainly determined by the formation and motion of vertical magnetic flux bundles. These bundles are formed when the initially horizontal magnetic field reconnects into a vertical configuration, effectively detaching from the black hole horizon. This reconnection occurs in a low-density, highly magnetized region on the equatorial plane that expands over time as more field lines undergo vertical reconfiguration. The resulting vertical flux tubes, filled with low-density plasma, are then transported outwards due to magnetic buoyancy. Our results present a detailed quantitative description of the morphology of MADs and of its evolution during flux eruptions, complemented by a description of the physical process by which excess magnetic flux is detached from the black hole, vertically reconfigured, and expelled.

AI.tldr: This study uses 3D GRMHD simulations to show that magnetic flux eruptions in black hole accretion disks enhance non-axisymmetric structures dominated by large-scale azimuthal modes. Vertical magnetic flux bundles form via reconnection, detach from the horizon, and rise outward, shaping the accretion flow morphology and explaining flux expulsion in MADs.
AI.motivation: To understand the azimuthal structure and evolution of the equatorial accretion disk around black holes during magnetic flux eruption events in 3D GRMHD simulations.
AI.method: Analyzing data from a standard 3D general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulation focusing on the equatorial slices of the accretion disk.
AI.result: Non-axisymmetric features are enhanced near the black hole during flux eruptions, dominated by low azimuthal modes (m=1, m=2). Vertical magnetic flux bundles are formed through magnetic reconnection, detach from the horizon, and transport outward by buoyancy, shaping the morphology of the magnetically arrested disk (MAD).
AI.conclusion: The morphology and evolution of the equatorial accretion flow close to the black hole are controlled by the formation and outward transport of vertical magnetic flux bundles formed by reconnection in low-density regions, which explains flux detachment and expulsion during flux eruptions in MADs.

title: Tracking ionization balance in intergalactic medium and its implications towards metallicity
comment: 15 pages, 11 figures, to be submitted soon
summary: Ionization balance in the intergalactic medium (IGM) is central to the interpretation of quasar absorption spectra, linking observed ionic columns to the underlying gas density, temperature, metallicity, and ionizing radiation field. Because ionization, recombination, and cooling timescales can be comparable to the timescales over which the ultraviolet background (UVB) and gas thermodynamic state evolve, ion populations may retain a strong memory of their past history. To this end, we present a fast, metals-inclusive, zero-dimensional framework for modeling the redshift evolution of the IGM. The model follows the coupled thermal and ionization evolution of a Lagrangian gas parcel in a redshift-dependent UVB, solving stiff, time-dependent rate equations for H, He, and 107 metal ions while self-consistently evolving the temperature through photoheating and standard cooling processes. We validate the framework against full three-dimensional hydrodynamical non-equilibrium calculations and find that it reproduces the thermal and ionization histories of the IGM with good accuracy over a wide redshift range, including the heating associated with $\rm He_{\,\rm II}$ reionization. As an application, we predict the cosmic $\rm C_{\,\rm IV}$ density parameter, $Ω_{\rm CIV}$, and use it to infer the origin of metal ions in the IGM and the corresponding metallicities from observational measurements, obtaining values broadly consistent with literature constraints. The framework is well suited for rapid parameter studies of how reionization timing, UVB spectral hardness, self-shielding, and UVB inhomogeneity shape the thermal and ionization history of the IGM and the resulting metal-line observables.

AI.tldr: Presented a validated, fast, metals-inclusive model for evolving the IGM's thermal and ionization state under a redshift-dependent UV background, enabling interpretation of metal-line observations and insights into metallicity and reionization effects.
AI.motivation: Understanding ionization balance in the intergalactic medium (IGM) is crucial for interpreting quasar absorption spectra and linking observed ionic columns to physical properties such as gas density, temperature, metallicity, and ionizing radiation.
AI.method: Developed a fast, metals-inclusive, zero-dimensional model that solves coupled thermal and ionization evolution equations for hydrogen, helium, and 107 metal ions in a redshift-dependent ultraviolet background (UVB), including photoheating and cooling processes, validated against full 3D hydrodynamical non-equilibrium simulations.
AI.result: The model accurately reproduces thermal and ionization histories of the IGM across a wide redshift range, including helium II reionization heating, and successfully predicts the cosmic C IV density parameter consistent with observational data and literature constraints.
AI.conclusion: This zero-dimensional framework provides an efficient and accurate tool to study how factors like reionization timing, UVB spectral hardness, self-shielding, and UVB inhomogeneity influence the IGM's thermal and ionization history and metal-line observables, facilitating rapid parameter studies.

title: A fast X-ray transient with chromatic flares: signatures of violent collisions induced by late-time central engine reactivation
comment: Submitted to ApJL
summary: Extragalactic Fast X-ray Transients (EFXTs) represent an emerging class of high-energy phenomena characterized by X-ray outbursts lasting from tens to hundreds of seconds. However, for more than half of the EFXTs, their physical origins remain elusive. In this Letter, we report the discovery of EP250302a, a luminous EFXT detected by the Einstein Probe (EP) at a redshift of $z = 1.131$. The multi-wavelength light curves of EP250302a reveal remarkable temporal features that distinguish it from the previously known EP-detected EFXT population, most notably a needle-like X-ray flare accompanied by smooth optical rebrightening during the afterglow phase. We suggest that the distinct X-ray and optical behaviors constitute the first observed instance of late-time violent collision of two relativistic shells in an EFXT. Drawing on insights from GRB studies, such a collision process strongly indicates the reactivation of a central engine, making EP250302a-like transients a unique laboratory for probing the late-time activity and jet physics of EFXT central engines.

AI.tldr: The study reports the discovery of EP250302a, a luminous EFXT with unique X-ray and optical features signaling late-time central engine reactivation, offering new insights into EFXT physics.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origins and central engine activities of Extragalactic Fast X-ray Transients (EFXTs), which remain largely unknown for many events.
AI.method: Discovery and multi-wavelength analysis of EP250302a using the Einstein Probe, focusing on its temporal X-ray and optical light curve features to identify unique behaviors.
AI.result: Identified a luminous EFXT at redshift z=1.131 with a distinct needle-like X-ray flare and smooth optical rebrightening, interpreted as a late-time collision of relativistic shells indicating central engine reactivation.
AI.conclusion: EP250302a represents the first observed case of late-time violent shell collision in EFXTs, providing a novel opportunity to study the late-time activity and jet physics of their central engines.

title: Euclid. Populating a dark universe with galaxies using SciPIC
comment: Submitted to A&A
summary: High-fidelity galaxy mocks are crucial for validating analysis pipelines and for cosmological inference. In this context, the Science Pipeline at PIC (SciPIC) is a pipeline specifically designed for the fast generation of synthetic galaxy catalogues from the halo properties identified in cosmological simulations. SciPIC delivers galaxy catalogues that aim to reproduce the observed luminosity function and clustering above a given flux detection limit over a wide redshift range. In this work, we introduce SciPICal, an automated pipeline that calibrates the parameters that set the main mock galaxy properties, namely number density, luminosities, colours, and positions. The pipeline is applied to the Euclid Flagship 2 Wide and Deep halo catalogues, specifically built to support the \textit{Euclid} wide and deep surveys. Compared to the recently released Flagship 2 Wide mock, our calibrated version improves the clustering predictions by approximately 50\% based on chi-squared values. Furthermore, we produce the Euclid Deep mock catalogue, which reaches up to $z = 10$ by populating a light-cone and a complementary snapshot at $z = 0$. We validate these catalogues using measurements from spectroscopic and photometric galaxy surveys, as well as with results from a hydrodynamical simulation. The obtained good agreement (within $15\%$ for most of the samples) in the clustering predictions across the different galaxy samples considered, validates our calibration strategy and demonstrates the strong predictive power of the generated mocks. This pipeline will allow us to improve the methodology applied in assigning the galaxy properties and ensures that the galaxy mocks remain up-to-date by incorporating constraints from upcoming observational data in the calibration procedure.

AI.tldr: This work introduces SciPICal, an automated calibration pipeline that significantly improves the accuracy of synthetic galaxy mocks used for cosmological inference, validated against observations and simulations, and applicable to Euclid survey data up to redshift 10.
AI.motivation: Generating high-fidelity galaxy mock catalogues is essential for validating analysis pipelines and improving cosmological inference.
AI.method: Development and application of an automated calibration pipeline, SciPICal, to tune parameters controlling galaxy properties such as number density, luminosities, colors, and positions using halo catalogues from cosmological simulations.
AI.result: Achieved approximately 50% improvement in clustering predictions for the Euclid Flagship 2 Wide mock catalogue, produced an extended Euclid Deep mock reaching up to redshift 10, and validated these mocks against observational surveys and hydrodynamical simulations with clustering predictions accurate within 15%.
AI.conclusion: The calibrated SciPICal pipeline enhances the predictive accuracy of synthetic galaxy catalogs and provides a robust, automated tool for updating mocks with observational constraints, thus supporting improved cosmological analyses for upcoming surveys.

title: GRB 210704A: A Luminous Fast Blue Transient in a GRB Afterglow at $z = 2.34$
comment: accepted by MNRAS, 24 pages, 24 figures, 4 tables
summary: We present detailed, multi-wavelength analysis of GRB 210704A: a Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor discovered and Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) detected gamma-ray burst (GRB). The burst is dominated by a short ($\approx 2$ s) pulse followed by weaker, softer emission. We line stack our afterglow spectrum and determine the most likely redshift to be $z = 2.34$. This is corroborated by the photometric redshift of the extended source underlying the GRB. The spectral energy distribution fit parameters, late-time imaging, as well as the GRB's energetics, spectral lag, and location point to a collapsar nature. Follow-up observations reveal excess optical/infrared emission with respect to a standard afterglow, peaking around $T_0 + 7$ d ($2$ d in the rest frame). The excess is extremely luminous ($M_{r} = -22.0$ mag) and rapidly evolving. Strikingly, it resembles the emission seen in recently discovered Einstein Probe fast X-ray transients EP241021a and EP240414a, as well as the population of luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs). This provides a link between these sources and GRBs. Fermi/LAT observations imply a high Lorentz factor, making this a case where LFBOT-like emission is also associated with a powerful successfully launched jet. We model the excess as likely coming from an energetic refreshed shock.

AI.tldr: GRB 210704A, detected by Fermi instruments, is a collapsar GRB at z=2.34 exhibiting an unusually bright, fast-evolving optical/infrared excess similar to LFBOTs, linking these transient classes and indicating an energetic refreshed shock as the emission source.
AI.motivation: To understand the multi-wavelength properties and nature of the gamma-ray burst GRB 210704A, and investigate its connection to other fast transients such as LFBOTs.
AI.method: Performed detailed multi-wavelength analysis using Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor and Fermi Large Area Telescope data, afterglow spectrum line stacking to determine redshift, spectral energy distribution fitting, late-time imaging, and follow-up optical/infrared observations.
AI.result: Determined GRB 210704A to be a collapsar-origin GRB at redshift z=2.34, with a high Lorentz factor jet, exhibiting an extremely luminous, rapidly evolving optical/infrared excess emission resembling LFBOTs and fast X-ray transients; modeled this excess as likely due to an energetic refreshed shock.
AI.conclusion: GRB 210704A links LFBOT-like optical/infrared emission to powerful GRB jets, demonstrating for the first time a connection between fast blue optical transients and successful GRB jets, with the excess emission likely originating from an energetic refreshed shock.

title: Microscopic primordial black holes as macroscopic dark matter from large extra dimensions
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables, comments are welcome
summary: We study the coupled cosmological evolution of primordial black holes (PBHs) and radiation in the Arkani-Hamed-Dimopoulos-Dvali (ADD) framework with $n$ large extra dimensions and a fundamental gravity scale $M_\star$ at the TeV scale. For PBHs with horizon radius smaller than the compactification scale, the higher-dimensional geometry implies a larger horizon size at fixed mass and therefore a suppressed Hawking temperature. As a result, radiation accretion can overcome evaporation in the early Universe and drive a ``runaway'' phase of rapid mass growth. By numerically solving the coupled mass and energy-density evolution equations, we show that for $n \geq 2$ initially microscopic PBHs with initial mass $M_i \gtrsim 10^{12}\,$g can grow by many orders of magnitude and potentially reach macroscopic, even solar-mass, scales by matter-radiation equality. We determine the critical initial abundance $β_{\rm crit}$ required for PBHs to account for the observed dark matter density and find that extra dimensions dramatically lower this threshold, allowing viable scenarios with $β_{\rm crit}\sim 10^{-44}$. This identifies a previously unexplored region of parameter space in which the dark matter abundance is achieved through dynamical mass growth rather than large initial collapse fractions.

AI.tldr: In the ADD framework with large extra dimensions, primordial black holes can grow rapidly from microscopic masses due to suppressed evaporation and dominant radiation accretion, enabling them to constitute dark matter at much lower initial abundances than previously thought.
AI.motivation: Investigate the cosmological evolution of primordial black holes (PBHs) interacting with radiation in the ADD framework with large extra dimensions and low fundamental gravity scale, to understand their role in dark matter.
AI.method: Numerical solution of coupled differential equations governing PBH mass and radiation energy-density evolution in a higher-dimensional geometry with $n$ large extra dimensions, focusing on horizon radius effects and Hawking temperature suppression.
AI.result: Found that for $n \geq 2$, initially microscopic PBHs with mass $M_i \gtrsim 10^{12}$ g can undergo runaway mass growth due to dominant radiation accretion over evaporation, potentially reaching solar-mass scales by matter-radiation equality. Determined a drastically lowered critical initial abundance $\beta_{\rm crit} \sim 10^{-44}$ for PBHs to explain dark matter density.
AI.conclusion: Extra dimensions in the ADD framework enable a unique cosmological evolution of PBHs characterized by runaway mass growth, allowing them to form a significant dark matter component from initially tiny populations, identifying a novel viable parameter space for dark matter scenarios.

title: Synchrotron-cooled plasma distribution in the outer magnetosphere of a neutron star
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures; ApJ in press
summary: The guiding center formalism is employed to analyze the motion of a charged relativistic particle in an inhomogeneous magnetic field, subject to magnetic mirroring and energy loss due to cooling. The governing equation for the evolution of the magnetic moment is derived. An example representing a neutron star (pulsar or magnetar) magnetosphere is presented to illustrate typical particle orbits. Notably, radiative losses are most pronounced near a trapped particle's turning point. Depending on the initial particle's pitch angle, energy loss can become catastrophic, resulting in the rapid migration of the particle into the loss cone and subsequent precipitation onto a neutron star. Conversely, particles with a larger pitch angle remain temporarily trapped and form a gradually decaying "cooled-loss-cone" or "funnel'' distribution, characterized by the maximum momentum space particle density being located at the edge of the loss cone. The size of the loss cone is energy-dependent and scales as $α_{c} \propto γ^{3/10}$. Synchrotron losses are strongest in a well-localized region of the magnetosphere, about a few hundred to a thousand star radii under typical pulsar and magnetar conditions. This region is a plausible site for synchrotron radiation originating in the outer magnetosphere, and could also be responsible for non-polar coherent pulsar emission, as well as weak fast radio bursts.

AI.tldr: Using guiding center formalism, the paper analyzes relativistic particle dynamics and energy losses in neutron star magnetospheres, revealing mechanisms of particle trapping, loss cone evolution, and identifying magnetospheric regions relevant for synchrotron emission and pulsar-related phenomena.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics of relativistic charged particles in neutron star magnetospheres, accounting for magnetic mirroring and energy loss mechanisms.
AI.method: The guiding center formalism is applied to derive the governing equations for particle motion and magnetic moment evolution in inhomogeneous magnetic fields with radiative cooling.
AI.result: Particles experience significant radiative losses near turning points; depending on initial pitch angle, they either rapidly precipitate onto the neutron star or become temporarily trapped, forming a cooled-loss-cone distribution with energy-dependent loss cone size. Synchrotron losses localize in specific magnetospheric regions, suggesting sites for various neutron star emissions.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a theoretical framework describing charged particle dynamics and energy loss in neutron star magnetospheres, identifying key regions responsible for synchrotron radiation and related astrophysical phenomena such as coherent pulsar emission and weak fast radio bursts.

title: Cosmology of Inelastic Self-Interacting Dark Matter: Linear Evolution and Observational Constraints
comment: 33 pages, 8 figures, 1 table
summary: We study the linear cosmological evolution of inelastic self-interacting dark matter in a two-component dark sector with a small mass splitting, assuming thermal initial conditions for the two species. We derive the coupled background and perturbation equations for inelastic conversion between the two species, considering both Power-law and Low-velocity saturation cross sections. Exothermic conversion injects kinetic energy into the light component, generating pressure support that suppresses small-scale structure and produces dark acoustic oscillations in the matter power spectrum. The resulting cutoff at scale $k > 1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ depends on the normalization and velocity dependence of the cross section, the dark matter mass and the mass splitting. Using linear power spectra computed with a modified Boltzmann solver, we apply recast constraints from Lyman-$α$ forest data and high-redshift UV luminosity functions, finding non-monotonic but closed exclusion regions driven by the competition between efficient conversion and rapid depletion of the heavy component. These results show that the internal thermodynamics of a secluded multi-component dark sector can leave observable imprints on structure formation, providing a complementary probe of dark matter beyond Standard Model interactions.

AI.tldr: This study shows that inelastic self-interacting two-component dark matter affects small-scale structure formation through energy injection and acoustic oscillations, constrained by astrophysical data, revealing new observational signatures of dark sector physics.
AI.motivation: To explore how inelastic self-interactions in a multi-component dark matter sector affect cosmological structure formation, addressing potential observable imprints beyond standard dark matter models.
AI.method: Derived coupled background and perturbation equations for two-component dark matter with inelastic conversions, considering Power-law and low-velocity saturation cross sections; computed linear matter power spectra using modified Boltzmann solvers; applied constraints from Lyman-α forest and UV luminosity data.
AI.result: Found that exothermic inelastic conversion injects kinetic energy causing pressure support, suppressing small-scale structure and inducing dark acoustic oscillations with a cutoff at certain scales; established exclusion regions on parameters due to interplay of conversion efficiency and heavy component depletion; demonstrated observable signatures in structure formation linked to dark sector interactions.
AI.conclusion: Inelastic self-interactions in a multi-component dark sector with small mass splitting imprint detectable features on cosmological structures, offering complementary probes to standard dark matter paradigms.

title: Ultrahigh-energy cosmogenic neutrino emissions in the high-redshift universe
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) revealed a large population of active galactic nuclei (AGN) with redshifts greater than five. We show that if they emit ultrahigh-energy protons with energies up to $\lesssim 10^{19}$ eV, the cosmogenic neutrino production in the high-redshift CMB field yields a neutrino flux with a bump at around 50~PeV. This flux is consistent with the current estimate of neutrino intensity from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. We argue that the predicted neutrino intensity naturally arises from the average AGN luminosity and number density observed by JWST, without the need for fine-tuning of relevant parameters. Future neutrino observations that confirm the 50-PeV bump and constrain the small-scale anisotropy will infer ultra-high energy cosmic-ray emissions in the early universe.

AI.tldr: High-redshift AGN observed by JWST could emit ultrahigh-energy protons producing a neutrino flux bump at 50 PeV, matching IceCube data and offering insight into cosmic rays in the early universe.
AI.motivation: The discovery of a large population of active galactic nuclei (AGN) at high redshifts by JWST suggests potential sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays and neutrinos in the early universe.
AI.method: The study models ultrahigh-energy proton emissions from high-redshift AGN and calculates the resulting cosmogenic neutrino flux produced through interactions with the cosmic microwave background (CMB).
AI.result: The predicted neutrino flux exhibits a characteristic bump at around 50 PeV, consistent with IceCube observations, without requiring fine-tuning of AGN luminosity or density parameters from JWST data.
AI.conclusion: The confirmed presence of the 50-PeV neutrino flux bump and constraints on anisotropy from future neutrino observations can serve as direct evidence of ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray production by early-universe AGN.

title: Nonperturbative stochastic inflation in perturbative dynamical background
comment: two columns, 22 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables
summary: Inflationary models that contain a transient ultra-slow-roll phase can exhibit strong non-perturbative dynamics, making the usual perturbative treatment of cosmological fluctuations incomplete. In such regimes, quantum diffusion and the nonlinear gravitational response of the background can both play important roles, motivating a framework that treats them systematically within quantum field theory in curved spacetime. In this work, we derive the first-order stochastic equations in quasi-de Sitter spacetime from the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism and develop a practical procedure to obtain compact stochastic equations that consistently incorporate metric perturbations via the classical Arnowitt-Deser-Misner equations. Our approach systematically captures classical non-perturbative effects while retaining the leading first-order quantum diffusion. We apply the formalism to two inflationary scenarios with an ultra-slow-roll phase, namely the Starobinsky piecewise-linear model and critical Higgs inflation. For the Starobinsky model, numerical lattice simulations validate the stochastic description and agree well with analytical results. For critical Higgs inflation, we find that the dynamics lead to a minor suppression of the power spectrum with an additional oscillation feature. Throughout, our analysis is restricted to the regime of small metric perturbations, ensuring the self-consistency of the perturbative stochastic treatment. These results establish a concrete bridge between first-principles quantum field theory in curved spacetime and the stochastic-$δN$ formalism for investigating non-perturbative inflationary dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a consistent stochastic framework from first principles to study ultra-slow-roll inflationary models, validated by applications to Starobinsky and Higgs inflation, bridging quantum field theory in curved spacetime and stochastic-$\delta N$ approaches.
AI.motivation: Inflationary models with a transient ultra-slow-roll phase induce strong non-perturbative dynamics, rendering traditional perturbative methods inadequate. There is a need for a framework that systematically treats quantum diffusion and nonlinear gravitational effects within quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
AI.method: The authors derive first-order stochastic equations in quasi-de Sitter spacetime using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. They develop a procedure to obtain compact stochastic equations that incorporate metric perturbations consistently through the classical Arnowitt-Deser-Misner equations, capturing classical non-perturbative effects and leading quantum diffusion.
AI.result: The formalism was applied to the Starobinsky piecewise-linear model and critical Higgs inflation. Numerical lattice simulations validated the stochastic description for the Starobinsky model, agreeing with analytical results. For critical Higgs inflation, a minor suppression of the power spectrum and an additional oscillation feature were observed. The analysis remains consistent by restricting to small metric perturbations.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a concrete connection between first-principles quantum field theory in curved spacetime and the stochastic-$\delta N$ formalism, providing a systematic and consistent approach for analyzing non-perturbative inflationary dynamics during ultra-slow-roll phases.

title: Systematic assessment of disk truncation in the black hole X-ray binary Swift J1727.8-1613 using NICER
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ (19+5 pages, 12+7 figures)
summary: The 2023/24 NICER monitoring campaign of the 7 Crab bright black hole X-ray binary Swift J1727.8-1613 covered the outburst in almost all accretion states. High-quality data are available in the high-Eddington-fraction hard-intermediate state, hard-to-soft transition, the soft state, and the poorly studied back-transition to the dim hard state, making it an ideal dataset to compare the accretion flow at vastly different accretion rates. We apply disk continuum fitting techniques to investigate the evolution of the inner disk radius throughout the outburst. Taking a temperature-dependent color-correction factor into account, we see evolution of the disk inner radius by a factor of a few comparing the hard states to the thermal/soft state. We tentatively detect an onset of disk truncation in the soft-to-hard transition, right after the source leaves the soft state. After accounting for model systematics, we find the disk to be more truncated in the high-luminosity bright hard state compared to the low-luminosity dim hard state.

AI.tldr: Study of Swift J1727.8-1613's 2023/24 outburst reveals inner disk radius varies with accretion state; disk truncation begins in soft-to-hard transition and is more significant at higher luminosities.
AI.motivation: To investigate the evolution of the inner disk radius in the black hole X-ray binary Swift J1727.8-1613 across different accretion states during its 2023/24 outburst.
AI.method: Applied disk continuum fitting techniques with a temperature-dependent color-correction factor to high-quality NICER data covering various accretion states during the outburst.
AI.result: Observed the inner disk radius changes by a factor of a few between hard states and the thermal/soft state, detected tentative disk truncation onset during the soft-to-hard transition, and found more pronounced disk truncation in the high-luminosity bright hard state compared to the low-luminosity dim hard state.
AI.conclusion: The accretion disk inner radius evolves significantly with accretion state, showing evidence of disk truncation varying with luminosity and accretion regime in Swift J1727.8-1613.

title: Neutrino self-interactions in post-reionization era: Lyman-$α$, 21-cm and cross-spectra
comment: 40 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: Neutrino self-interactions delay the onset of free-streaming in the early universe, leaving distinct, scale-dependent signatures on the matter power spectrum. We investigate these signatures in post-reionization 21-cm intensity mapping and the Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest at redshifts $z \sim 2$--$3.5$, and forecast the constraints achievable with upcoming surveys using Fisher matrix analysis. Modeling neutrino self-interactions through an effective four-fermion parameterization with coupling $G_{\rm eff}$, we compute modifications to the Ly$α$ and 21-cm auto- and cross-power spectra for both strongly interacting (SI$_ν$, $\log_{10}G_{\mathrm{eff}} = -1.77$) and moderately interacting (MI$_ν$, $\log_{10}G_{\mathrm{eff}} = -5$) scenarios. We then combine these with forecasts for a representative next-generation cosmic microwave background (CMB) mission to evaluate the capabilities of SKA1-Mid and PUMA. We find that the Ly$α$--21-cm cross-correlation provides a systematics-resilient probe of the interaction signal, and decisively breaks the degeneracy between the primordial scalar power spectrum amplitude ($A_s$) and $G_{\rm eff}$ that limits CMB only analysis, particularly for the SI$_ν$ mode. Furthermore, the CMB+PUMA combination emerges as the optimal survey configuration for both regimes, reaching 1$σ$ constraints of $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$ on $σ(\log_{10}G_{\rm eff})$ for the SI$_ν$ mode and $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$ for the MI$_ν$ mode. Compared to the CMB-only baseline, this represents an improvement of approximately one order of magnitude for the SI$_ν$ mode, and nearly two orders of magnitude for the MI$_ν$ mode. We show that this conclusion holds uniformly over the full range of coupling strengths from $\log_{10}G_{\rm eff} = -6$ to $-1.77$.

AI.tldr: The study forecasts that combining Ly$\alpha$ forest and 21-cm intensity mapping with future CMB surveys can greatly improve constraints on neutrino self-interactions in the early universe, breaking key parameter degeneracies and achieving up to two orders of magnitude tighter limits than CMB data alone.
AI.motivation: The paper is motivated by the need to understand the signatures of neutrino self-interactions in the early universe, specifically their impact on the matter power spectrum and large-scale structure observables post-reionization.
AI.method: The authors model neutrino self-interactions using an effective four-fermion coupling parameterized by $G_{\rm eff}$, compute modifications to the Ly$\alpha$ and 21-cm auto- and cross-power spectra, and perform Fisher matrix forecasts combining these with next-generation CMB data from SKA1-Mid and PUMA surveys.
AI.result: They find that the Ly$\alpha$--21-cm cross-correlation effectively breaks degeneracies present in CMB-only analyses, improving constraints on $G_{\rm eff}$ by up to two orders of magnitude. The CMB+PUMA survey combination yields $1\sigma$ constraints on $\log_{10}G_{\rm eff}$ of order $10^{-3}$ for strongly interacting and $10^{-2}$ for moderately interacting neutrino scenarios, robust across a wide coupling range.
AI.conclusion: Combining post-reionization large-scale structure probes (Ly$\alpha$ and 21-cm) with next-generation CMB data substantially enhances sensitivity to neutrino self-interactions, offering a systematics-resilient and powerful avenue to constrain the effective four-fermion coupling parameter beyond CMB-only limits.

title: Influence of winds on shocked magnetized viscous accretion flows around rotating black holes
comment: 17 pages, 10 figures, 1 table, To appear in the Astrophysical Journal
summary: We study global transonic solution for a relativistic, magnetized, viscous advective accretion flow around a rotating black hole, incorporating the effects of mass and angular momentum loss through winds. Our model considers dominant toroidal magnetic fields with synchrotron radiation as the primary cooling mechanism. To self-consistently model mass loss, the mass accretion rate is prescribed to decrease inward as a power-law with disk radius. With this, we solve the governing equations that describe the accretion flows in presence of winds and obtain the flow structure in terms of the inflow parameters (energy $\mathcal{E}$, angular momentum $λ$, plasma-$β$, accretion rate $\dot{m}$, and viscosity $α_{\rm B}$), the wind parameters ($p$, governing mass loss; and $l$, governing angular momentum transport by winds), and the black hole spin ($a_{\rm k}$). Our analysis reveals that winds substantially modify the accretion flow leading to a significant decrease in disk luminosity. We specifically identify global solutions that admit standing shocks and find that winds profoundly alter shock properties, such as the shock radius ($x_{\rm s}$), compression ratio ($R$), and shock strength ($S$). Furthermore, we determine the critical wind parameter $p^{\rm crit}$ beyond which steady shock solutions cease to exist. We demonstrate that increased viscosity and strong angular momentum extraction by winds lead to reduce $p^{\rm crit}$. These findings evidently highlight a complex interplay between viscosity and winds in governing the dynamics of shock formation in accretion disks.

AI.tldr: This study models transonic relativistic, magnetized accretion flows around rotating black holes including winds and viscosity effects, revealing winds reduce luminosity and modify shock properties. Critical wind parameters for shock existence and the interplay between viscosity and winds are identified.
AI.motivation: To understand the effects of winds and viscosity on the dynamics of relativistic, magnetized advective accretion flows around rotating black holes, particularly on shock formation and disk luminosity.
AI.method: Develop a global transonic accretion flow model incorporating toroidal magnetic fields, synchrotron cooling, and mass/angular momentum loss through winds, solving governing equations with prescribed inward-decreasing accretion rate and wind parameters to analyze flow structure and shock properties.
AI.result: Winds significantly reduce disk luminosity and alter shock characteristics (radius, compression ratio, strength). A critical wind parameter is identified, beyond which steady shocks vanish. Increased viscosity and angular momentum extraction by winds lower this critical value, showing complex interactions affecting shock dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Winds play a crucial role in shaping accretion flow dynamics, especially shock formation and disk emission, with viscosity and angular momentum loss from winds intricately influencing the existence and properties of shocks in magnetized accretion disks around rotating black holes.

title: Gravitational-wave lensing beyond rays: a disordered-system approach
comment: 26 pages, plus technical appendices, 2 figures
summary: We develop a framework to describe gravitational wave propagation through a stochastic distribution of weak gravitational lenses beyond the geometric optics limit. We model the lens distribution as a static random background field and formulate the problem in the language of quenched disorder, treating the disorder averaged density matrix as the fundamental object from which observables are computed. Using the Schwinger Keldysh formalism, we construct a path-integral representation of the averaged density matrix and derive its explicit form perturbatively for a suitable class of couplings. The result naturally separates into a quadratic exponential term, which governs the suppression of phase sensitive contributions in the averaged description, and a purely oscillatory contribution, which modifies coherent propagation through a disorder-induced correction to the propagation kernel. This provides a unified description of interference, diffraction, and statistical fluctuations of the lens distribution within a single framework. We also identify the physical scales controlling the onset of coherence loss and illustrate the formalism in the case of Gaussian wave packets. More generally, the derivation applies to any system described by the same class of actions, making the framework relevant beyond gravitational wave lensing to wave propagation in disordered media.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a perturbative path-integral framework using quenched disorder and the Schwinger Keldysh formalism to describe gravitational wave propagation through stochastic weak lenses beyond geometric optics, capturing coherence loss, interference, and diffraction effects applicable to waves in disordered media.
AI.motivation: To develop a comprehensive framework describing gravitational wave propagation through weak gravitational lenses beyond the geometric optics approximation.
AI.method: Model the lens distribution as a static random background, use the language of quenched disorder, employ the Schwinger Keldysh formalism to construct a path-integral representation of the disorder-averaged density matrix, and derive perturbative expressions for observables.
AI.result: Obtained an explicit perturbative form of the averaged density matrix separating into a quadratic exponential term causing phase suppression and an oscillatory term modifying coherent propagation. Identified physical scales for coherence loss and demonstrated application to Gaussian wave packets.
AI.conclusion: The framework unifies interference, diffraction, and statistical fluctuations of lens distributions in gravitational wave propagation and is applicable to general wave propagation in disordered media.

title: Deeper analysis of Fermi-LAT unassociated 4FGL J2112.5-3043 for possible identification
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures
summary: In the 4FGL-DR4 point-source catalog of the Large Area Telescope (LAT) onboard NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Observatory (Fermi-LAT), around a third of the sources are still unidentified (unIDs). In this work, we perform a detailed study of one of them, namely 4FGL J2112.5-3043. Only gamma-ray emission has been detected from this unidentified source, with no counterpart observed at any other wavelength as of today. Together with its high detection significance, this makes 4FGL J2112.5-3043 a particularly compelling target for further investigation. The results of our spectral and spatial analyses show that the source photon spectrum is better described with a subexponential cutoff power-law spectral model, with no significant flux variability over time, and a morphology consistent with being a point-like source. We investigate and discuss the characterized emission within the context of both conventional and exotic astrophysics, namely a pulsar origin or potential dark matter (DM) annihilations in a nearby Galactic subhalo. Although our results are inconclusive and neither confirm a DM origin nor firmly establish an astrophysical nature, we find a spectral preference for the $b\bar{b}$ and $c\bar{c}$ DM annihilation channels over a pulsar origin, thus making this unID a particularly intriguing candidate for next multiwavelength observations.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the gamma-ray source 4FGL J2112.5-3043, finding spectral evidence favoring dark matter annihilation over a pulsar source but remains inconclusive, highlighting it as a key target for future observations.
AI.motivation: A third of sources in the 4FGL-DR4 Fermi-LAT catalog remain unidentified, including source 4FGL J2112.5-3043 which only exhibits gamma-ray emission with no counterparts at other wavelengths, motivating detailed study to clarify its nature.
AI.method: Performed detailed spectral and spatial analyses of 4FGL J2112.5-3043, examining its gamma-ray emission characteristics, flux variability, and morphology to compare with astrophysical and dark matter annihilation models.
AI.result: The source spectrum is best described by a subexponential cutoff power-law with no significant variability and point-like morphology; spectral features favor dark matter annihilation channels $b\bar{b}$ and $c\bar{c}$ over a pulsar origin, but results remain inconclusive.
AI.conclusion: 4FGL J2112.5-3043 remains an unidentified gamma-ray source with characteristics that make dark matter annihilation a plausible explanation, though further multiwavelength observations are needed to definitively determine its nature.

title: A simple relation: Neutron star magnetic field strength and spectral shape at low mass accretion rates
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. In press at Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary:
The X-ray spectra of neutron stars with moderate magnetic fields ($B\sim 10^{12}$ G) in high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) at low X-ray luminosities ($L_\mathrm{X}\lesssim 10^{35}$ erg/s) are characterized by a double humped shape. This shape has been explained either as the radiation from a two-temperature magnetized atmosphere, where thermal radiation dominates at soft X-rays below about 10 keV, and cyclotron radiation with an imprinted cyclotron line dominates at high energies, or by the complex redistribution of primary X-rays in a structured atmosphere.
  The theoretical explanations of the double humped structure predict the spectra to depend on the magnetic field. We aim to connect the model predictions with observations.
  We analyzed archival NuSTAR observations of four HMXBs consisting of a neutron star and a Be star (BeXRBs), with known magnetic fields at luminosities low enough to show the characteristic double-hump spectrum. We modeled these spectra empirically and derived a relation between the energy of the intersection of the two humps and the magnetic field strength. In a second step, we tested whether this correlation is supported by fitting synthetic spectra simulated with the physically self-consistent polcap model.
  We find a linear correlation between the magnetic field strength and the intersection energy for the real BeXRB NuSTAR spectra and polcap-based simulated NuSTAR spectra alike.
  The effect of the magnetic field on spectral formation results in an observable correlation between the field strength and spectral shape. This derived positive correlation between intersection energy and magnetic field strength also allowed us to roughly estimate the magnetic field strength. Additional observations of XRBs and dedicated modeling efforts will be necessary to determine whether this approach is valid beyond the B-field range that was tested in this work.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies and validates a linear correlation between the magnetic field strength of neutron stars in high-mass X-ray binaries and a characteristic spectral feature (intersection energy of a double-humped X-ray spectrum) using NuSTAR observations and synthetic polcap models, enabling magnetic field estimation from spectral data.
AI.motivation: The study aims to link theoretical predictions of the double-humped X-ray spectrum shapes in neutron stars to actual observational data, focusing on how the spectral shape depends on the magnetic field, to validate models and enable magnetic field estimation.
AI.method: Archival NuSTAR observations of four BeXRBs with known magnetic fields at low luminosities were analyzed. Spectra were empirically modeled to find a correlation between intersection energy of the double humps and magnetic field strength. This was validated by fitting synthetic spectra produced by the polcap model, a physically self-consistent spectral simulation.
AI.result: A linear correlation was found between the magnetic field strength and the intersection energy of the two humps in the X-ray spectra, both in observed BeXRB data and polcap-simulated spectra. This correlation implies that spectral shape can be used as a proxy to estimate magnetic field strength in neutron stars under certain conditions.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic field significantly influences the X-ray spectral formation in neutron stars, producing an observable correlation between spectral features and field strength. This correlation can be leveraged to estimate the magnetic field in HMXBs, though further observational and modeling efforts are necessary to confirm the approach beyond the tested magnetic field range.

title: A Generalized Algorithmic Framework for Detecting Faraday Rotation Measure Flares in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts
comment: 6 pages and 1 figure. Comments welcome!
summary: Variations in the Faraday rotation measure (RM) of repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide critical diagnostics of the dynamically evolving magneto-ionic environments surrounding their progenitors. Sudden, transient ``RM flares'' can trace the passage of discrete magneto-ionic structures, such as stellar coronal mass ejections from the companion or other dense plasma clumps, across the line of sight. However, identifying these rare events is difficult because RM evolution manifests a wide range of complex behaviors, from smooth, long-term trends to chaotic stochasticity, further complicated by highly non-uniform temporal sampling. This complexity makes it a non-trivial challenge to distinguish localized physical flares from intrinsic environmental volatility. We present a generalized algorithmic framework that establishes a statistically robust methodology for the automated detection and characterization of RM flares. By objectively isolating discrete transient perturbations from quiescent backgrounds, this pipeline enables the first uniform census of environmental variability across the FRB population. Applying this framework to 15 repeating FRBs, we find that high-confidence RM flares are remarkably rare, with FRB 20220529A being the only source to exhibit a statistically significant event under standardized parameters. Other active repeaters instead display high-level intrinsic fluctuations or secular evolution. This work provides a rigorous foundation for distinguishing between different modes of local plasma dynamics, offering a crucial diagnostic tool for identifying the diverse progenitor systems and local environments of FRBs.

AI.tldr: This study introduces a robust algorithm to detect transient Faraday rotation measure flares in repeating FRBs, finding such events are rare and demonstrating a method to distinguish discrete magneto-ionic disturbances from general environmental variability around FRBs.
AI.motivation: The paper is motivated by the need to detect and characterize rare, transient Faraday rotation measure (RM) flares in repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs), which provide insights into the magneto-ionic environments around FRB progenitors but are difficult to identify due to complex RM behavior and irregular temporal sampling.
AI.method: The authors develop a generalized algorithmic framework to automate the robust detection and characterization of RM flares by isolating discrete transient perturbations from background RM variability, enabling an unbiased census of environmental RM variability in repeating FRBs.
AI.result: Applying the framework to 15 repeating FRBs, the study finds that statistically significant RM flares are rare, with only FRB 20220529A showing a clear event. Other sources exhibit intrinsic fluctuations or secular trends without discrete RM flares.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the developed statistical pipeline effectively distinguishes localized RM flares from intrinsic environmental volatility, providing a crucial diagnostic tool to differentiate plasma dynamics modes and characterize diverse FRB progenitor environments.

title: Localization and Confidence Region Estimation of Short GRBs with the COSI BGO Shield Using a HEALPix-Based Deep Learning Approach
comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, proceedings of the ADASS XXXV (2025) conference, to appear in ASP Conference Serie
summary: The Compton Spectrometer and Imager is a NASA satellite mission under development that will survey the entire sky in the 0.2-5 MeV range using a wide-field germanium detector array, surrounded on the sides and bottom by active shields (the Anticoincidence Subsystem, ACS). The ACS aims to suppress and monitor background events, as well as detect transient sources, such as Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs), through its onboard triggering algorithm. The data related to GRBs are sent to the ground and analyzed by an automated pipeline to localize the GRBs and share their positions with the community. In this work, we present a brief GRB localization method based on ACS data, utilizing deep learning (DL) techniques, which can estimate the 90\% confidence region, including cases where it is split into multiple areas. To address this, we developed a neural network classifier that predicts the GRB location as a probability distribution across the sky map following the HEALPix framework. The distribution can be used to compute the 90\% confidence regions. Future work will compare this DL-based localization approach with classical methods such as $χ^2$ fitting and Maximum Likelihood Estimation.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a deep learning approach using a neural network classifier to localize Gamma-Ray Bursts detected by NASA's Compton Spectrometer and Imager, estimating 90% confidence regions on the sky map and setting the stage for comparison with classical statistical localization methods.
AI.motivation: The need to improve the localization of Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) detected by the Anticoincidence Subsystem (ACS) on the Compton Spectrometer and Imager satellite to enhance rapid and accurate position dissemination.
AI.method: Use of a neural network classifier employing deep learning techniques to predict the GRB location as a probability distribution across a HEALPix sky map; this allows estimation of 90% confidence regions, including complex cases with multiple disjoint areas.
AI.result: A brief GRB localization method was developed that leverages ACS data and deep learning, capable of producing 90% confidence regions for GRB positions; future comparisons with classical methods are planned.
AI.conclusion: Deep learning-based classification of ACS data can effectively localize GRBs with quantified confidence regions, offering a promising alternative to traditional statistical methods for sky localization.

title: Las Cumbres Observatory Gravitational-Wave Follow-up in O3 and O4: Strengths and Weaknesses of a Rapid Response Galaxy Targeted Strategy
comment: To be re-submitted to AAS Journals following a first referee report. Comments welcome
summary: We present a summary of gravitational-wave (GW) follow-up using the Las Cumbres Observatory global network of telescopes during the third (O3) and fourth (O4) observing runs of the GW detectors. As in O2, we implemented the Gehrels et al. 2016 galaxy-targeted strategy. Here we test its efficacy in O3 and O4 and analyze the Las Cumbres Observatory response time and depth for nine GW alerts that showed a possibility of having an electromagnetic counterpart (GW190425, GW190426_152155, S190510g, GW190728_064510, GW190814, S190822c, GW191216_213338, S240422ed and S250206dm). We find that Las Cumbres Observatory is able to begin observations in response to GW alerts within minutes of the alert, with the observations being deep enough to detect possible GW170817-like kilonovae out to a median distance of 250 Mpc. In this sense a global rapid-response network of telescopes like Las Cumbres is an excellent GW follow-up facility. However, the galaxy-targeted follow-up strategy was much less efficient in O3 and O4 than originally predicted, given the larger than assumed GW localizations. We conclude that coordination between various facilities to include both wide-field and rapid-response capabilities is required to achieve efficient and comprehensive follow-up of GW events.

AI.tldr: The Las Cumbres Observatory network quickly and deeply responds to GW alerts but galaxy-targeted follow-up was less efficient in recent runs; coordinated efforts combining wide-field and rapid-response telescopes are necessary for effective GW event follow-up.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the effectiveness of the galaxy-targeted follow-up strategy for gravitational-wave events during recent observing runs and assess the capabilities of the Las Cumbres Observatory global telescope network.
AI.method: Implemented the Gehrels et al. 2016 galaxy-targeted strategy for follow-up; analyzed response time and observation depth of Las Cumbres Observatory for nine GW alerts potentially having electromagnetic counterparts during O3 and O4 runs.
AI.result: Las Cumbres Observatory can begin observations within minutes of GW alerts, reaching depths sufficient to detect kilonovae similar to GW170817 at median distances of 250 Mpc. However, the galaxy-targeted strategy was less efficient in O3 and O4 due to larger-than-expected GW localizations.
AI.conclusion: A global rapid-response telescope network like Las Cumbres is an excellent GW follow-up facility, but efficient and comprehensive follow-up requires coordination of both wide-field and rapid-response observatories to overcome limitations of galaxy-targeted strategies.
